cases.text: The guest number is only an estimate.
cases.fact: The audience has not confirmed attendance.
cases.next_step: Label the estimate and name the staff check.
cases.staff_note: Do not contact guests from this lesson.

cases.text: A menu item has a festive name but no ingredient list.
cases.fact: The name does not establish ingredients.
cases.next_step: Ask the trained adult to check current written information.
cases.staff_note: Never infer an allergy-safe item from its name.

cases.text: Eight guests each need one item. Packs hold four.
cases.staff_note: These are task numbers, not an actual order.

cases.text: Two packs cost £3 each. The task budget is £12.
cases.next_step: Show the working and keep unused money as a balance.
cases.staff_note: No real purchase or fundraising target is set.

cases.text: The proposed table blocks the walking route.
cases.next_step: Move the paper table plan and ask staff to check access.
cases.staff_note: No unapproved room setup is required.

cases.text: A possible visitor cannot be confirmed.
cases.fact: There is no confirmed external participant.
cases.next_step: Use a staff audience and paper service rehearsal.
cases.staff_note: Keep visitor or placement status unconfirmed.

Purpose and success checks
The weekly scheme line above is shared across two lessons. This lesson focuses on a festive café proposal.
What would a workable catering plan need?
I can plan for a proposed audience. I can work out a simple task cost. I can list what staff still need to confirm.
VOC-W6-L1-E1: Individual festive catering proposal with proposed audience/purpose, quantity and fictional cost working, role allocation, pending checks and an in-class alternative.
Before pupils arrive

Print the fictional planning brief and price table in Support Cards. Use paper only, a calculator if appropriate, empty sample containers and a clear table plan. There is no confirmed event date, guest, visitor or placement. Staff retain responsibility for any later real-event permissions and food-safety plan.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.
Calendar and continuity

Monday 7–Friday 11 December 2026. Two 40-minute lessons this week. No teaching day or clock slot is inferred. Any visitor, placement or external audience is unconfirmed; the in-class route is ready to use.
Staff enter the actual teaching date above. Continue the accepted prior-week evidence and support routines.

B. A plan is a proposal. The responsible adult must confirm any real audience, venue, timing, budget, ingredient/allergen information and safe arrangements. Reteach by sorting “proposed” and “confirmed” details. No booking is inferred from a planning sheet.
Access and practice
Supported: choose and explain one option. Independent: add quantities, costs and roles. Aspire: explain a limit or a change in need.

Use the independent task brief: eight proposed guests, one item each, packs of four at £3, task budget £12. Two packs cost £6, leaving £6. This is a fictional planning allowance, not live pricing or permission to spend. Plan customer communication, accessibility, quantities, roles, hygiene/allergen checks, storage and clearing up. Keep all operational details proposed or pending.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Planning only: no purchasing, cooking, serving or invitations. Actual ingredients, allergen requirements, hygiene, equipment and storage need responsible-adult checks before a real service. No “allergy-free” assurance or ingredient substitution is guessed.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. Keep the event as a paper proposal. An adult acts as the audience for questions; use fictional needs and the printed task prices. No external participation is needed.
Assessment and feedback

Task calculation: 8 items need 2 packs of 4; 2 × £3 = £6; £12 − £6 = £6 remaining. Accept a reasoned different quantity only when its assumptions and full recalculation are explicit. Menu names never establish allergen safety. No real booking, spending or event completion is claimed.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Fictional plan: six guests, two items each. 6 × 2 = 12 items in the practice plan. Three packs of four cost £2 per pack. 3 × £2 = £6 for the practice items. A £10 task budget leaves £4. Guests and food checks still need approval.

B. A plan is a proposal. The responsible adult must confirm any real audience, venue, timing, budget, ingredient/allergen information and safe arrangements. Reteach by sorting “proposed” and “confirmed” details. No booking is inferred from a planning sheet.
Individual evidence key

Task calculation: 8 items need 2 packs of 4; 2 × £3 = £6; £12 − £6 = £6 remaining. Accept a reasoned different quantity only when its assumptions and full recalculation are explicit. Menu names never establish allergen safety. No real booking, spending or event completion is claimed.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Do not contact guests from this lesson.
Card B: Never infer an allergy-safe item from its name.
Card C: These are task numbers, not an actual order.
Card D: No real purchase or fundraising target is set.
Card E: No unapproved room setup is required.
Card F: Keep visitor or placement status unconfirmed.
Common misunderstandings
A proposed menu does not confirm guest needs. A budget is a limit, not an instruction to spend it all. A food name cannot tell us every ingredient or allergen.
Teaching boundary

Planning only: no purchasing, cooking, serving or invitations. Actual ingredients, allergen requirements, hygiene, equipment and storage need responsible-adult checks before a real service. No “allergy-free” assurance or ingredient substitution is guessed.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
